sections.title: Mocked sign-in and shared data
sections.what: Replaces the sign-in check with a switchable user, and creates three users, a crew, an invite code and a match.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets each test act as a member, an outsider, or someone signed out.
sections.watch_out: The mock must keep the same export names as the real auth module.

sections.name: authz: crew and contest membership
sections.title: Crew and contest access rules
sections.what: Checks members can read their crew and contests, outsiders get not found on every read, missing crews look the same, lists are scoped, joining twice is a conflict, and routes and pages behave correctly.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the existence of private crews hidden from outsiders.
sections.watch_out: Returning 404 instead of 403 is intentional here, and changing it would reveal which crews exist.

summary: Tests that crew and contest data is visible only to members, that non-members and missing crews both get not found, and that route handlers require a session.
purpose: Protects private crew data from outsiders.
why: Likely reason: outsiders should not learn which crews exist, so missing and forbidden crews look the same.
how: Mocks the auth module so the current user can be switched, and the sign-in check fails when no user is set. Creates an owner, a member, an outsider, a crew, an invite code and a match. Checks members can read the crew, its members and contests. Checks non-members get not found on seven reads. Checks a missing crew looks the same. Checks crew lists show only the caller's crews. Checks a repeat join is a conflict and an unknown code is not found. Checks route handlers return 401 without a session, scope results, reject a blank name with 400, and create a crew with 201. Checks the page helper turns a non-member into a 404.
inputs: Test users, a crew and a match created in setup.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: The auth mock replaces the real module, so its exported names must match. The 404 design is deliberate and changing it would reveal which crews exist.
debug: If an outsider sees data, check each service read for the membership check. If a route returns the wrong status, check the session handling.
